narrative.overview:
Each lesson is one calm page of prose: a single centered column on white, opened by a quiet line of facts (week, lesson number, minutes) and a plain, heavy title. Nothing frames the text. The index rail sits to the left as a soft gray panel that holds the course, the reader's progress, and the outline of the lesson being read, so the page itself carries nothing but the lesson.

The system was rebuilt at the owner's request because the earlier worksheet look (black frames, ruled header strips, a second display face) felt heavy and cluttered. What remains is subtraction: one family, one accent, soft fills and hairlines instead of outlines, and a small set of gentle corners. Hierarchy comes from size and weight. The only expressive material left is the hand-drawn sketch figures, which keep their rough.js strokes and their fixed diagram inks.

Legibility leads. Text sits on flat white or a near-white fill, never on a pattern or an image; secondary text is a gray that clears AA on every surface it uses.
keyCharacteristics: White page, quiet #f7f8fa index rail, no textures anywhere.
Inter for headings, interface and reading; JetBrains Mono for code; Kalam only inside sketch diagrams.
One left edge for everything: prose at about 75 characters per line, with figures, tables, code and calculators extending wider.
No boxed strips, no heading rules, no black frames; soft fills, hairlines, small radii.
One accent (Ballpoint Blue) for links, focus and marks; a solid ink primary button.
Hand-drawn sketch figures with one meaning per ink.

readingPrinciples.name: One family.
readingPrinciples.body: Inter sets headings, interface and body. Mono appears only for code and calculator values; the hand font appears only inside sketch diagrams.

readingPrinciples.name: Body at 16 to 18px, line height 1.6 to 1.75.
readingPrinciples.body: Lesson body is 17px at 1.7 on every width.

readingPrinciples.name: About 65 to 80 characters per line, with figures on the same edge.
readingPrinciples.body: Type scales from 17px to 19px with the screen and the prose column is 36em of it, so a full line stays about 75 characters. Figures, tables, code and calculators share its left edge and extend to the wide measure; portrait diagrams stay at the text width.

readingPrinciples.name: Hierarchy from size and weight, not from boxes or rules.
readingPrinciples.body: Headings are larger and heavier; they carry no underline, overline, frame or fill.

readingPrinciples.name: At most one accent colour.
readingPrinciples.body: Ballpoint Blue is the accent. The diagram inks belong to figures and calculator readouts only; Margin Red is a small position mark, not a second accent.

readingPrinciples.name: Secondary text at AA contrast.
readingPrinciples.body: Secondary Ink is about 6.4:1 on white, 5.9:1 on the soft fill and 6.0:1 on the rail; in dark it is about 8.7:1 on the page.

readingPrinciples.name: Generous vertical space between sections.
readingPrinciples.body: Section headings open with 2.4em above them; the sign-off sits 56px below the lesson.

readingPrinciples.name: No chrome that does not help the reader.
readingPrinciples.body: Every box, line or label must carry information or an action. If it only decorates, it goes.

rules.name: The Clear Ground Rule
rules.body: Text always sits on flat white, the rail gray, or the soft fill. No grids, patterns, gradients, or images behind text.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Ballpoint Blue is the only interface accent. Diagram inks stay inside figures, calculators and the two tinted callouts; Margin Red marks position and nothing else.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Inter carries every heading, control and paragraph. A second family never enters for emphasis or display.

rules.name: The Counted Things Rule
rules.body: Counts, tallies, scores, lesson numbers and calculator results use tabular figures so columns line up.

rules.name: The Shared Edge Rule
rules.body: Prose keeps the text measure; figures, tables, code and calculators share its left edge and take the wide measure. Nothing is centred on its own axis.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: Separate with a soft fill or a Hairline, never with a blur shadow, gradient or translucency on content.

rules.name: The Mark Shape Rule
rules.body: Type and state are told apart by shape, not colour alone: a drawn tick for done, a struck cross and strikethrough for a wrong answer, and a distinct small mark before each callout label (square, triangle, dot, dash, double bar).

dos: Do set everything in Inter, with body at 17px and 1.7 line height.
Do keep text, tables, code and figures on one left edge: prose at the text measure, wide blocks at the wide measure.
Do make hierarchy with size and weight alone.
Do use the soft fill or a Hairline to set a block apart, with a radius from the 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12px scale.
Do keep secondary text at Secondary Ink or darker.
Do give every new state a distinct mark shape before giving it a colour.
Do swap tokens in place for dark mode using the `*-dark` values.
donts: Don't put a rule, border or fill on a heading.
Don't frame content in black or Ink outlines.
Don't add a second family for display, labels or emphasis.
Don't put a small uppercase label or category kicker above a heading; the meta line holds facts only.
Don't add a second interface accent; diagram inks stay in figures and calculators, and Margin Red marks position only.
Don't use blur shadows, gradients, or translucent content surfaces.
Don't add a right margin, sidebar or panel beside the reading column.
